nodes.description: Loss of normal KREMEN1 function deregulates canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. KREMEN1 has context-dependent biphasic activity in the DKK1-KREMEN-LRP5/6 system, and patient cells show elevated baseline Wnt activity with a blunted response to WNT3A rather than a simple uniform increase or decrease.

evidence.reference_title: KREMEN1 Variants Associated with Ectodermal Dysplasia Impair Complex Formation of KREMEN1 with DKK1 and LRP6 and Attenuate WNT3A Response.
evidence.snippet: Primary fibroblasts from the 3 patients with KREMEN1 pathogenic variants showed a higher WNT pathway activity under starved culture condition that was followed by attenuated signaling response to WNT3A, suggesting a more general WNT pathway deregulation.

evidence.reference_title: Novel homozygous KREMEN1 mutation causes ectodermal dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Kremen potentiates Wnt/β-catenin signaling by maintaining LRP5/6 at the plasma membrane in the absence of Dickkof1 (Dkk1); however, Kremen increases Dkk1-mediated Wnt inhibition in the presence of Dkk1

nodes.description: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling is required for the epithelial-mesenchymal interactions that drive development of ectodermal appendages, including tooth germs and hair follicles. Deregulated Wnt signaling from KREMEN1 loss disrupts this morphogenesis, producing tooth agenesis and hair defects.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of KREMEN1, a modulator of Wnt signaling, is responsible for ectodermal dysplasia including oligodontia in Palestinian families.
evidence.snippet: The Wnt signaling pathway is critical to development of ectodermal structures.

nodes.description: Disease-associated KREMEN1 missense variants are under-glycosylated (especially O-glycosylation) and form the KREMEN1-DKK1-LRP6 ternary complex less efficiently than wild-type KREMEN1, while binding of KREMEN1 to LRP6 alone is preserved.

evidence.reference_title: KREMEN1 Variants Associated with Ectodermal Dysplasia Impair Complex Formation of KREMEN1 with DKK1 and LRP6 and Attenuate WNT3A Response.
evidence.snippet: Ternary complex formation of all 4 KREMEN1 protein variants with DKK1 and LRP6 was reduced compared with that of wild type, whereas formation of the KREMEN1-LRP6 complex was not affected by the nonsynonymous variants.

evidence.reference_title: KREMEN1 Variants Associated with Ectodermal Dysplasia Impair Complex Formation of KREMEN1 with DKK1 and LRP6 and Attenuate WNT3A Response.
evidence.snippet: KREMEN1 wild type was extensively N- and O-glycosylated, whereas the 4 protein variants showed a significant reduction in glycosylation, in particular of O-glycans.

nodes.description: Biallelic KREMEN1 variants reduce or abolish functional KREMEN1 protein. Null alleles (such as a splice-donor variant triggering nonsense-mediated decay) eliminate the protein, while missense alleles in the extracellular domains reduce its activity as a DKK1/LRP5/6 receptor. The founder alleles are mostly homozygous, but compound-heterozygous genotypes also occur.

nodes.description: Management of ECTD13 is symptomatic and centers on the oligodontia: early multidisciplinary dental and prosthodontic care, including removable prostheses, overdentures, and later dental implants, to restore function and appearance. There is no disease-modifying therapy that targets the Wnt pathway defect, and no treatment-specific outcome evidence is reported in the KREMEN1 case series, so no evidence snippet is attached to this row.
